The only factor that affect radioactivity is TIME  -   They can pass through opaque materials unlike visible light  -   They unique gases   through which they pass, causing them to fluorescence.  -   Enormous amount of energy is always released.  -   Radioactivity is natural phenomenon.  -   However, it can now be induced artificially.  -  Different between nuclear reactions and chemical rea ctions  Nuclear reactor   Chemical reaction  -   The element is destroyed   The element is not destroyed  -   it involves the Nucleus   Electrons are responsible  -   enormous amount of energy is  involved  Energy   release is quite small  The Isotopes of the same element have  i.   The same chemical properties because they have the same atomic number  ii.   Different physical properties because of the different in the neutron number  iii. CATHODE RAY   -   TUBE  (i)   Gases do   not conduct electricity at ordinary air pressure.  (ii)   However, they will conduct electricity if the pressure is reduced & the voltage is  increased.  (iii)   As J.J Thompson kept reducing the pressure and increasing the voltage, the  gas in the tube began to florescent.  (iv)   After a while, the gas began to glow green.  (v)   At this point, he concluded that the glow was due to some kind of rays which  travelled in straight lines from the cathode.  (vi)   He called these rays cathode rays.  (vii)   But with further Analysis, he called the cathode rays   ELECTRON which had  been predicted by some scientist.  PROPERTIES OF CATHODE RAYS  1.   They travelled in straight lines from the cathode to the Anode.  2.   They cost shadows of opaque objects placed in their path.  3.   They are negatively charged particles.  4.   They are   capable of producing mechanical motion.  5.   They are identical in nature and in their ratio of charge to mass irrespective of the  nature of the residual gas in the discharge tube or metal, used as the cathode.  THE DISCOVERY OF PROTON  (i)   J.J Thompson used a centr ally perforated cathode.  (ii)   He noticed a reddish glow in the opposite direction to the green glow moving to  the anode.  (iii)   He proved that this reddish glow was due to positively charged rays which he  later called protons.

No matter what metal the cathode is  made of or the residual gas   in the tube,  the rays have the same charge to mass  ratio  The rays are identical.  They must be basic constituents of  matter  2. An objects placed in front of the anode  cast a shadow at the screen  The rays travelled in straight lines  5.   The rays pass through a thin foil of  aluminum through which hydrogen atom  The rays must be smaller than hydrogen  atoms. They are sub   –   atomic particles

RUTHERFORD’S ATOMIC MODEL   (A THIN GOLD FOIL)  NOTE  -   Marsden and Geiger at Rutherford’s instruction bombarded a thin gold foil by  alpha ( ∝ ) particles positively charged particles.  -   Most of the particles were not   deflected showing that the atoms consist largely of  empty space.  -   Some of the particles, however, were deflected side wards and some backwards  through large angles when they pass very close to the positively charge nucleus.  -   Rutherford explained that the ato m has a dense centre where the protons and the  neutron are concentrated.  -   He also suggested that electrons move round the Nucleus

INTERPRETATION  When an electron of an atom in its ground state absorbs a photon of energy (from  light or radiation).  It will jump to a level of high or energy. The electron is then said t o have been  excited.  -   When the electron returns to its ground state, it emits the Quantum of energy  (photo)  Which it absorbed initially  -   These emission of energy produces a series of lines in the emission spectrum.  Using hydrogen to explain the   electron spectra, the series of lines obtained are  Lyman , balmer, Pasche   Brackett   and pfund   . Lyman is found in the  ultra violet region while balmer in the visible region.  Bracket is found in the in fra red and the others in the far infra -   red regions  HEISENBERG UNCERTAINITY PRICIPLE  This explains the character of an electron. He states that if we mention the  momentum of an electron accurately then we cannot know its position with certainty  and vice versa.  -   This makes electrons very elusive (not field)  -   T he wave mechanical model does not restrict electrons to define electron around  the Nucleus like Niel Bohr’s model.  -   Instead, it makes the electron elusive and indicates a region around the Nucleus  called an orbital.  - Niel Bohr’s model could only work for h ydrogen atom.

,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,, HINTS ON CHEMISTRY PRACTICALS  An exceptional chemistry material you probably have not   read!  546  PAULI EXCLUSIVE PRINCIPLE  Two electrons in the same shell or orbital cannot have the same value for all the four  quantum Numbers.  -   This means electrons in an atom cannot behave in the same way.  -   The electrons in a given shell do not have th e same amount of energy.  -   This is because electrons move about the nucleus at different speed.  -   However, they have approximately equal energy.  -   The main energy level corresponds to the energy electrons have due to their  distance from the Nucleus.  -   Electrons   within a shell have minute energy different due to:  i.   Their angular momentum (shape)  ii.   Their orientation in space (magnetic)  iii.   Their clockwise or anti clockwise spine.  THE WAVE MECHANICAL MODEL  The orbital is identified by a set of four quantum number which i ndicate where there  is the probability of finding an electron with a certain amount of energy.  i. The principal quantum shell  ii. The Azimuthal or subsidiary quantum  iii. The spine quantum shell  iv. The magnetic quantum shell  PRINCIPAL QUANTUM SHELL (n)  These are the shells.  This has integral values of n =1, 2, 3, 4 which   corresponds to K,L, M, N etc.  -   It gives the total energy in a shell.  -   The minimum possible number of electrons in a shell is given by 2n 2 .  SUBSIDIARY QUANTUM SHELL  (OR SUB SHELL)  -   It has integral values ranging from 0 to n - 1  -   The electrons with the   subsidiary Quantum number (0, 1, 2, 3) are usually  referred to as spdf respectively.  -   The sub shell gives the number of energy division in each shell  Subshell   Max electrons  S   2  P   2 + 4 =6  D   6 + 4 =10  F   10 + 4 = 14  Shell   Subshell
